plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Trim SMH, SPY, and QQQ to reduce concentration.
Increase allocation to QQQI for income.
Add to CRWD as a quality tech holding.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation by cutting leverage and reducing sector bets.
It aims for a steady, low-drawdown return profile.
conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for ~1.5% monthly return by focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentrates holdings in less volatile assets, accepting lower potential upside for lower risk.

plan: Trim SOXL and SPAL, sell SPAL completely.
Reduce SMH, SPY, and QQQ to lower concentration.
Buy NVDA and AAPU as strong, high-potential longs from the scanner.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth opportunities.
It aims to reduce overall leverage while adding high-conviction names.
The goal is risk-first growth with a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% monthly return by blending risk reduction with growth. It trims concentrated positions and some leverage while adding promising scanner setups. Expect moderate upside with controlled drawdowns.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs SOXL and SPAL.
Trim SMH, SPY, and QQQ to reduce concentration.
Buy NVDA and AAPU, focusing on top scanner setups.
This plan aggressively pursues growth by increasing leverage and concentration.
It aims to capture upside from high-conviction, high-potential names.
Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% monthly return by leaning into leverage and high-conviction setups. It increases leveraged ETFs and adds top scanner names while still trimming some existing concentrations. Be aware of amplified gains and losses, and the daily rebalancing decay of leveraged ETFs.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs and high-beta single names (SOXL, SPAL, SMH, CRWD).
Significantly increase QQQI allocation for monthly distributions.
Add to SPY and QQQ for broad market exposure and potential income.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income over growth.
It aims to park capital in yield-generating assets with low volatility.
NAV can still fall in a selloff, but distributions are the primary goal.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets ~1% monthly return by prioritizing consistent distributions. It cuts all high-beta and leveraged assets, shifting capital into income-oriented ETFs and broad market indices. While aiming for low drawdowns, NAV can still decline in market downturns.
